title: Profiles reference auth.users by uuid
claim: user_profiles.user_id is a uuid foreign key to auth.users with ON DELETE CASCADE and a unique (org_id, user_id).
note: The unique (org_id, user_id) is what D98 (§19.40) will relax for multi-role.
opinion: add-test (sql): cheap to prove directly — assert the FK, the CASCADE and the unique index in one migration test rather than leaving a foundational constraint unproven.

title: The capacity cap is read from org settings, default 1.0
claim: check_operator_capacity reads orgs.settings capacity_cap, defaulting to 1.0. Configurability is proven by the 1.1-peak case, refused at cap 1.0 and accepted at 1.2.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/20_capacity_test.sql
opinion: Solid: the sql test drives both the default and the 1.0/1.2 boundary the claim actually asserts.

title: Child rows reference their parent by composite (org_id, id)
claim: Parents carry unique (org_id, id) and children reference (org_id, id), so cross-tenant row stitching is structurally impossible.
note: §19.18 found nodes.level_id was the one plain FK and added the composite in migration 0014.
opinion: add-test (sql): the composite-FK cross-tenant isolation claim is cheap to pin and a regression here is a silent security leak.

title: Two runs on one cell may not overlap in time
claim: runs carries an exclusion constraint on (node_id, timerange) for non-cancelled rows, so a run move onto an occupied window is refused by the database with run_overlap.
opinion: add-test (sql): an exclusion-constraint invariant this important (no overlapping runs on a cell) deserves a direct assertion that run_overlap actually fires.

title: An assignment has exactly one of run_id or product_id
claim: A CHECK enforces exactly one of run_id and product_id, and a trigger forces a run-attached assignment's node_id to equal its run's node, refusing a half-completed cross-cell move.
opinion: add-test (sql): the CHECK-plus-trigger pairing is two mechanisms working together — exactly where an untested regression hides.

title: nodes.path is derived by trigger and cascades on rename or move
claim: Callers never set path. A trigger slugifies the name onto the parent path and an AFTER UPDATE OF name, parent_id trigger rewrites every descendant's path.
opinion: add-test (sql): path cascade on rename/move is core to the whole hierarchy and deserves its own dedicated migration test.

title: org_id is carried on every child table for uniform RLS
claim: shifts, shift_breaks, node_shift_templates, operator_skills and node_skill_requirements all carry org_id.
opinion: Low priority: a schema-completeness statement that mainly enables the RLS requirements around it (R-D8, R-D107 family); a standalone test would be redundant — accept-risk or fold into a migration lint.

title: Operators, products, skills readable org-wide; nodes and writes grant-scoped
claim: Under RLS any user in the org can read operators, products and skills, so a conflict message can name a cell outside their grant. Subtree grants restrict which nodes are visible and all writes.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/40_rls_test.sql
opinion: Solid: 40_rls_test.sql is the right shape of proof for a read/write-scope claim like this.

title: Audit log is admin-read-only, written by trigger
claim: audit_log rows are written by a SECURITY DEFINER trigger on runs and assignments only, are readable only by admins, and a no-op update (only updated_at changed) writes no row.
opinion: add-test (sql): the no-op-update-writes-no-row clause is the subtle part and regresses silently — worth a dedicated case.

title: Shifts in a template never overlap; resolution is a DB function
claim: Non-overlap of shifts within a template is an exclusion constraint, and nearest-ancestor resolution is provided by resolve_shift_template(node).
opinion: add-test (sql): same shape as R-D4 — an exclusion constraint plus a resolver function, cheap to pin with a handful of cases.

title: The board renders in UTC through one seam
claim: BOARD_ZONE in src/features/board/lib/time.ts is the only place the zone is known and no component calls a local-time Date method. Every day is exactly 1440 minutes.
note: D88a (§19.21) makes the board axis site-local in Phase 2; D13 still describes what v1 ships.
opinion: Superseded by R-D88.

title: The board window is always whole days
claim: The date control picks dates and board_window is called with midnight-to-midnight instants, so day boundaries fall at exact multiples of 1440 minutes from the window origin.
opinion: add-test (vitest): a pure function over board_window's midnight boundaries is cheap to unit test and easy to break with an off-by-one.

title: x is minutes since windowStart; previous day's shift tail drawn
claim: Horizontal position is minutes since the window start over a computed windowMinutes. Shift geometry loops from day −1 so an overnight shift from the day before the window appears on the first morning.
opinion: add-test (vitest): the geometry math is pure and is literally the codebase's own "pure, testable module" — it just has no test yet.

title: Three zoom levels with fixed pixel and snap values
claim: Compact 64 px/h, Standard 104, Fine 168 with snaps 60, 30 and 15 minutes; Standard is the default.
opinion: Low priority: a constant table (pixel/snap per zoom level). A snapshot test is cheap but silent-regression risk is low; accept-risk is defensible.

title: The board opens on today with a 3-day window
claim: The default window starts at the start of today's UTC day and spans 3 days. The original Monday-of-the-week anchor was a seed concern that leaked into the product and was reversed.
opinion: add-test (vitest): the note that this default was already "reversed" once means it's regressed before — worth pinning so it can't drift back quietly.

title: A node is a track row iff its level is schedulable
claim: Track rows are exactly the nodes on the schedulable level; indentation comes from path depth. Nothing hardcodes department, line or cell.
opinion: add-test (vitest): likely exercised incidentally by treeView.test.ts, but nothing here names it directly — a short direct assertion would close the gap cheaply.

title: Row windowing is hand-rolled from prefix sums, no virtualization library
claim: Row heights are computed from lane packing, not measured, so visible rows are found by prefix-sum offsets and a binary search in a pure, testable module.
opinion: add-test (vitest): the claim itself says this was built as "a pure, testable module" — that module has no listed test, the clearest gap in this file.

title: A reverted edit's toast names the block
claim: When a drag is reverted the toast reads like "Widget X 06:00–14:00 — reverted". Capacity, eligibility and run-overlap errors already name the operator or cell and go through the one error path; every other error gets the block label prefixed.
note: §18.6: popover-fired mutations still toast without a label; needs runById/assignmentById.
opinion: Low priority: a toast-copy requirement — a wrong string is cosmetic, not correctness; accept-risk is fine short-term.

title: Density is a manual setting
claim: Board density (Comfortable, Standard, Compact) is chosen manually from the toolbar.
note: Amended in §18.10 to add Fit as default and removed entirely by D75 (§19.7).
opinion: Superseded by R-D75.

title: A chip can be re-parented between runs or detached to direct
claim: An existing assignment can be moved to another run or detached to a direct assignment by patching run_id and product_id through the existing field-edit path, with no second write path.
opinion: add-test (sql or vitest): re-parenting/detaching through the existing field-edit path is real business logic and deserves a direct test.

title: Node paths are unique per org
claim: (org_id, path) carries a unique index, so two roots cannot share a name and sibling names that slugify alike are refused. This closes the grant leak where a grant on one node matched another with a byte-identical path.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql
opinion: Solid: the unique-index test directly proves the claim and closes a real grant-leak scenario.

title: A node can never become its own ancestor

verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql
opinion: Solid: the anti-cycle trigger is proven directly.

title: A node sits one level below its parent, same structure

title: The level list is saved whole; array index is the position

verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql
opinion: Solid: the whole-array contract is proven by the same suite that exercises reordering.

title: move_node re-parents only and never changes a node's level
claim: The new parent must be exactly one level above the node's existing level; a move that would silently promote or demote is refused with level_mismatch.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql | cases N17
opinion: Solid: case N17 pins the specific level_mismatch refusal described.

title: The schedulable flag cannot move while scheduled work exists

verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql | cases L12
opinion: Solid: case L12 is a direct hit on the claim.

title: delete_node deactivates a whole subtree or deletes only an unused leaf
claim: Mode deactivate cascades to the subtree; mode delete refuses while the node has children, runs or assignments. A NULL or unknown mode must never fall through to delete.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql | cases D1–D3
opinion: Solid: both branches plus the dangerous NULL/unknown-mode case are covered.

title: Hierarchy RPCs raise named codes, never raw constraint errors
claim: path_collision, node_cycle, level_mismatch, level_in_use, node_in_use and schedulable_level_locked join the closed set (twelve codes in all), every one PT409. RPCs pre-check and raise a named code, and malformed arguments such as NULL or an unparseable id return a closed-set code rather than 23502 or 22P02.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql
opinion: Adequate but loose: the claim lists twelve named codes but verified_by cites no case ids, so it's not clear every code in the closed set is actually exercised — worth a quick audit of the test file rather than a new one.

title: Fit is the only density mode
claim: The three manual density buttons are removed. The fit mechanism remains and restoring the control is re-adding one button group.
opinion: add-test (vitest): a negative claim (three buttons removed) — cheap regression guard against someone re-adding the control.

title: Chrome uses --chrome-scale, never --ui-scale
claim: Anything outside the fitted scroll container that consumes vertical space (header, toolbar, app shell, status lines) scales with the viewport-driven --chrome-scale. --ui-scale reaches only fitted content. Otherwise fit feeds back into its own input and oscillates.
verified_by: vitest | src/test/scaleAudit.test.ts
opinion: Solid: scaleAudit.test.ts is built exactly for this class of claim.

title: Portaled floating panels are chrome; the drag ghost is not
claim: Popovers and the toast stack scale with --chrome-scale in every dimension, not just font-size. The drag ghost stays on --ui-scale because it is a preview of a fitted block.
opinion: add-test (vitest): scaleAudit.test.ts already covers the sibling --chrome-scale claims — this one looks like an oversight, cheap to add there.

title: Node read and edit checks are scoped to the caller's org
claim: app_can_read_node and app_can_edit_node resolve the node together with its org, so an admin or a grant in one org can never read or write another org's runs, assignments or nodes even when paths are identical.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/80_cross_org_test.sql | cases C1–C7
opinion: Solid: C1–C7 is a direct, thorough proof of the cross-org boundary.

title: Scaling is the unit: rem surfaces on a scaled root
claim: :root font-size is 100% times --chrome-scale, guarded by @supports with a plain default, and new surfaces size in rem. Breakpoints stay in px. The board keeps calc(px * scale) because its geometry is computed in pixels.
verified_by: vitest | src/test/scaleAudit.test.ts
opinion: Solid, same scaleAudit.test.ts suite.

title: nodes_select keeps an admin short-circuit that reads no table
claim: The nodes SELECT policy is org_id = app_current_org() and (app_is_admin() or app_can_read_node(id)). The app_is_admin() term must answer without reading nodes, or INSERT ... RETURNING cannot see its own row and create_node breaks for everyone.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql | cases N1
opinion: Solid: case N1 precisely pins the exact failure mode described.

title: Each site may have its own hierarchy shape
claim: Levels belong to a named, org-scoped hierarchy template. One org can run Site › Department › Line › Cell at one plant and Site › Line at another, scheduling at different depths. A node's template is its level's template and a tree never straddles two templates.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/90_hierarchy_template_test.sql | cases T6, T7
opinion: Solid, T6/T7 in the hierarchy template suite.

title: create_node takes a template id for a root node
claim: create_node accepts p_template_id. For a root it is required when the org holds more than one template and defaults to the only one otherwise; for a child the level is resolved within the parent's template. A root must never land in an arbitrary template.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/90_hierarchy_template_test.sql | cases T20–T28, T30–T32 ;; vitest | src/test/shapePicker.test.ts
opinion: Solid: both the sql side and the client picker are covered.

title: Per-site timezone: site-local axis, wall-clock shifts, Phase 2
claim: The board axis is the site's local time (D88a). A shift keeps its posted wall-clock start across a DST change, so it is 7 or 9 hours that day (D88b). The timezone hangs off a node, resolved nearest-ancestor with an org fallback. Scheduled for Phase 2 (D88c); nothing new may assume UTC.
opinion: Reasonable to leave uncovered for now — explicitly Phase 2 work with three sub-claims; flag so it isn't forgotten when that phase starts.

title: Form controls inherit font and body is sized in rem
claim: input, button, select, textarea and optgroup inherit font and letter-spacing globally, and body font-size is 0.8125rem, so every control scales with the root and forgetting a class costs a border, never the typeface or size. Every admin stylesheet is a rem surface.
verified_by: vitest | src/test/scaleAudit.test.ts
opinion: Solid, scaleAudit.test.ts.

title: Tree grouped by Site Structure with a level label per row
claim: The section is named Site Structure and the picker merges into the Levels card. Rows are grouped by template (heading only when the org holds more than one), every row shows its level name, a row with an unresolvable level lands in a trailing group rather than disappearing, and vertical guide rails show ancestry.

opinion: Solid: the grouping and fallback-group cases map directly onto the claim.

title: No RLS-scoped read is issued before the identity is settled
claim: Query hooks take a required enabled flag driven by canQueryAsUser(userId, loading), and screens show a spinner while the session resolves. Only null means nobody; an empty-string id is an identity.
verified_by: vitest | src/test/session.test.ts | cases Q1–Q6
opinion: Solid: a precise, well-targeted suite for a subtle race condition.

title: A level save that would strand nodes is refused
claim: After writing the new order, save_hierarchy_levels checks the real rows: every root in the template sits at position 0 and every child sits one below its parent. Either failing raises level_in_use and aborts, leaving the stored order untouched. Phrased as an outcome so a scrambled structure can still be repaired.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql | cases L1, L1b, L13–L17
opinion: Solid: covers the strand-refusal both ways.

title: Every RPC is explicitly revoked from PUBLIC and anon
claim: Every function in the API surface carries REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC and anon alongside GRANT to authenticated, and every migration that creates or recreates a function carries its own grant block.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/70_hierarchy_test.sql | cases L17 ;; sql | supabase/tests/75_node_mobility_test.sql | cases M29

title: Siblings reorder by drag, placed before or after a row
claim: Dragging a node between two siblings reorders it. The top and bottom bands of a row mean place before or after as a sibling; the middle band adopts. An insertion caret is shown, a noop canDropOn result is legal for a pure reorder, and a same-level refusal is worded as an unsupported reorder, not a lecture about levels.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/75_node_mobility_test.sql | cases M1–M8
note: The server half (place_node) is built and tested; the client gesture is P1-5l, not yet built within §19.0–§19.43.
opinion: Solid: covers the reorder/adopt/refusal shape well.

title: Whole row drags with a mouse; handle alone on touch
claim: For mouse and pen the whole tree row is the drag source with a ~4px movement threshold so clicks stay clicks; on touch only the ⠿ handle drags so the page stays scrollable. The handle remains visible as the affordance. The level list gets drag-to-reorder (moveTo) in the same build, sharing one pointer mechanism.
opinion: add-test (e2e or vitest): touch-vs-mouse drag source and shared pointer mechanism are exactly the kind of gesture code that silently breaks.

title: System admin, site admin, supervisor: no lurking
claim: A system admin has all powers on any site; a site admin changes only the site they belong to; a supervisor edits assignments only and has no access to the admin page. Admin functions must ask "admin for this node?" rather than "admin at all?".

The row is left as the maintainer stated it rather than quietly edited; the correction lives here, and `requireAdmin.test.tsx` G3b pins the current behaviour so nobody restores a refusal the server would contradict.
opinion: Needs reword before it needs a test: the note already flags one clause as out of date (supervisor now DOES reach the admin page per D114) — fix the wording first.

title: A role belongs to a (person, scope) pair
claim: A person can hold several roles case by case, for example supervisor in one scope and admin in another, by carrying a role on each grant row instead of one role per profile. The cross-org escalation must be closed before multi-role is switched on.
opinion: add-test (sql), but gate it on the cross-org escalation fix the requirement itself names as a precondition — testing now would pin a known-unsafe state.

title: One drag surface for every screen, by default

No drag surface names `--signal-ok` directly or re-declares a shared rule; every token a surface reads is defined.

title: Shift patterns are per-site, with company defaults
claim: Shift patterns belong to a site; a site admin sets up their own site's patterns, a company admin may seed a default pattern that sits alongside them. Which pattern a node runs is still resolved by nearest ancestor up the tree; ownership decides who may edit a pattern, not which one applies.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/51_shared_list_owners_test.sql | cases Q0–Q37 (shift_templates, shifts, shift_breaks policies)

title: A product's colour belongs to whoever owns the product
claim: A product stores its colour as a palette token name, never a hex; the column is NOT NULL and is filled on insert with the least-used token within the owner's scope, so inserting a product never changes an existing product's colour. title: Where a thing belongs decides where it is offered

It is offered at every node at or below its owner and nowhere else; offering is a union across owners (a node offers many products), the ancestor test is by ltree label not string prefix, and the client mirror fails open. Company-wide was the everywhere fallback.

title: Tickets are called trainings, and a training has a record

title: What you can set once, you must be able to change

title: A control may not be named after less than it does

verified_by: vitest | src/test/productsPanel.test.tsx | cases T1–T7

title: Ownership decides who may read, not only who may edit
claim: A shared row is readable when it is company-wide, or when its owning node and one of the reader's grants lie on the same branch in either direction — a grant on Line 1 reads Plant 1's rows, a grant on Plant 2 does not. Company admins read everything. Dependents follow their parent: shifts their template, breaks their shift, `operator_skills` the operator. The `org_id` term stays inside every policy.

title: There is no company-wide row
claim: `site_node_id` is NOT NULL on `products`, `operators`, `skills` and `shift_templates`. title: Ownership scopes any level; nothing is assigned outside it

title: Delete keeps the past
claim: Deleting a product or person removes it from the list and from anything not yet started; completed and started runs keep their record of it. title: Admin-ness and org are derived from one deterministic acting profile
claim: app_current_profile_id() picks one profile by ORDER BY org_id, id; app_current_org(), app_is_admin() and app_can_write() all derive from that profile. A user who is viewer in one org and admin in another can never write in the org where they are a viewer, and still can write where they are admin.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/45_acting_scope_test.sql | cases A1–A11

title: CSV import: RFC 4180, BOM stripped, parents before children
claim: The import parser handles quoting, BOM and CRLF, maps headers, detects duplicates and orders tree rows parents-before-children. A re-import must update existing rows rather than fail with path_collision.
opinion: Check whether CSV import for nodes has actually shipped — if not, this is a queued feature, not a tested-vs-untested requirement.

title: Three roles: system admin, site admin, supervisor/viewer
claim: A system admin (org-wide `user_profiles.role = 'admin'`) can affect anything at any site. A site admin is a `profile_grants` row with role `admin` on a site node and may change only that site. A supervisor holds a `supervisor` grant, may only do assignments and has no admin page. A viewer grant reads only. The role vocabulary is admin | supervisor | viewer.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/46_scoped_roles_test.sql | cases S1–S19 (S2 pins the role check constraint)
opinion: Solid.

title: A person may hold several roles, one per place
claim: A role is a property of a (person, place) pair, not of a person. Multiple roles are multiple `profile_grants` rows on different nodes; the key `(profile_id, node_id)` allows exactly one role per person per node. A supervisor on Line 3 who is also admin on Plant 2 is two grants.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/46_scoped_roles_test.sql | cases S5, S13, S15
opinion: Solid.

title: Grants add power and never subtract it
claim: Coverage is the union of every grant whose node is an ancestor-or-self of the row, and the strongest role wins. Admin on Plant 1 plus viewer on Line 3 makes the person an admin on Line 3; giving someone read access to one line can never demote a plant admin.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/46_scoped_roles_test.sql | cases S7
opinion: Solid.

title: `app_is_admin_anywhere` is visibility only, never authorisation
claim: `app_is_admin_anywhere()` answers only "should this person see the admin section at all". It never authorises a write.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/46_scoped_roles_test.sql | cases S13, S14
opinion: Solid.

title: Node visibility follows grant paths; creators see their new row
claim: `nodes_select` admits a row when the org matches and the caller is a system admin or the row's path is at-or-below one of the caller's grant paths. The predicate reads the row's own `path` column, never the `nodes` table, so an `INSERT … RETURNING` by a site admin or supervisor returns the created row instead of D85's silent empty result.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/46_scoped_roles_test.sql | cases S10, S18
opinion: Solid, and the "reads the row's own path column" detail is exactly the subtlety these hierarchy bugs live in.

title: A permission refusal says `not_permitted`, not a wrong code
claim: When a site admin is refused because a node is outside their grant, the error is `not_permitted`. title: Each site is its own instance of the app
claim: A company (system) admin reaches every site and may change anything anywhere. title: Shared lists carry an owning site; NULL means company-wide

title: A new site gets its own copy of a structure

title: One site, one structure, owned by a root

title: Permission is checked after existence, not before

title: A tree row offers peer slots or adopt, never both

Roots are siblings of each other and can be reordered by a company admin.

title: Client hides only what the server refuses, and vice versa
claim: A client control is never hidden for something the server permits, and never shown for something the server refuses. Fixes to a permission defect land on the server first; a screen is turned on only when the policies behind it allow the edits it offers.
verified_by: sql | supabase/tests/65_offered_in_window_test.sql | cases X1 the defect in one comparison — the same person, part and cell, with the readable place list EMPTY and the server answering TRUE; X2 every part on a supervisor's board names her cell in offered_node_ids while site_node_ids stays empty (so a later fix that widened the read policy instead would move that number rather than pass quietly); X3 the answer is still per node; X4–X6 the SECURITY DEFINER helper discloses nothing the caller could not already read — not a root above their grant, not a sibling department, not the other tenant, which uses the same paths ;; vitest | src/test/scope.test.ts | cases XP1 a part whose places were filtered away is still offered, XP2 an empty places list is not the question any more, XP3 an empty OFFERED list is offered nowhere, XP4 (promoted from DEF-0002's pin) a part made only at another plant is absent, XP5 a part on another line is absent, XP6 the answer is per node ;; vitest | src/test/auditAccess.test.tsx | cases the rail offers what the server permits, tab by tab -- a site admin IS offered Settings, is NOT offered Activity, and a company admin gets both, so no case passes by hiding everything
note: ⛔ CONTRADICTED 6 Sept by DEF-0015 (tester): a viewer granted one cell presses Enter on the track and gets a create form with a four-person picker and an enabled Create, and clicks the chip and gets Person, Save and Delete --- every one refused by the policies (the DELETE came back 200 with zero rows and the board said "You don't have permission to change that. --- reverted."). The panel and Copy week ARE hidden; the pop-ups are not decided by can_place at all. Minor: nothing is written and the app says why. ⚠️ FIX-CLAIMED in `01a2612` (session 81). Decided in one place: the board reads `can_place` and hands it to the gesture layer (no create form on Enter or click-drag, no drag) and to the assignment and run pop-ups as read-only (the details and Close). Nine unit cases, the pin green, and a browser case as Viva, the new Plant A viewer, reading it off the screen. ✅ VERIFIED 6 Sept by the tester (session 82), in the browser as Viva, Vito and Vina with every write intercepted: no panel, no Copy week, Enter on a track opens nothing, the chip and the run band open read-only with Close only, a drag and an arrow nudge attempt no request. Ana and Dana lost nothing: the create form, Person/Save/Delete, the run's fields, the drag and the nudge all still fire. The gate is the server's `can_place`, read once; six mutations of it each caught by name. An invariant stated in `shapePicker.ts`, `siteAccess.ts` and verification rule 8c; individual instances are covered by their own entries. ⚠️ FIX CLAIMED, NOT VERIFIED (DEF-0005, fix 808a52d). This row has now been broken in BOTH directions by the same picker, which is why it finally has cases of its own. DEF-0002 was the first half — a control SHOWN for something the server refuses, eight parts of twelve. DEF-0005 was the second — a control HIDDEN for something the server permits, three parts of four, and worse, because a refusal is loud while a missing option is silent. The second was not a regression from the first: it dates to migration 0034 and was invisible to every role that could report it, since an admin's own grant covers everything their board can show. ⚠️ AND A THIRD TIME, FROM THE HIDDEN SIDE AGAIN (DEF-0007, VERIFIED 2026-09-05, fix 23ba9aa). The Settings tab was hidden from every plant admin while `set_node_setting` was taking their writes on their own plant. Same shape as DEF-0005 and the same reason it stayed: the client's rule was a BOOLEAN CONSTANT written when the server's rule was one too, and the server's became per-node two migrations later. A flag on a menu row cannot track a predicate that takes an argument. The lesson this row now carries three times over: where the server's gate names a NODE, the client's answer belongs where the node is known, not on the rail. ⭐ The tester re-verified it on the screen and at the server: Dana is offered Settings and not Activity, all three of the panel's scopes behave as its header says, and a legal value written over her own session was READ BACK OUT OF THE DATABASE rather than trusted because nothing threw. Both halves of the axis were mutated on a scratch copy and both go red with a name, so the replacement for the case that used to pin the bug is not itself a case that cannot fail. ⛔ A FOURTH TIME, FROM THE HIDDEN SIDE, ONE LEVEL DEEPER (DEF-0010, open). DEF-0007 was a PLANT admin refused the Settings tab. The tab is reachable now and the scope it can be pointed at is still a PLANT ROOT --- so somebody whose ADMIN grant sits on a LINE or a CELL gets the whole rail, lands on "Company defaults" with both controls disabled and "Only a system admin can change this", and reaches none of the panel's three states. Measured over that person's own session with the rows read back: `set_node_setting` takes their write on their own line AND on a cell below it, and refuses the plant root above them; `board_window` emits `node_policies` PER NODE, so a line-level answer is the one the board enforces there. The client predicate is not the bug --- `canAdministerPlant` mirrors the server exactly --- the bug is that `SettingsScope` has no way to name a place below a root, and `settingsScope` sends a reader who cannot write the company to the company anyway. ⚠️ AND THIS ROW'S OWN EVIDENCE HAS A HOLE IN IT (DEF-0009): the third `verified_by` entry above names `src/test/defects/DEF-0007.test.tsx`, which `cab45d9` deleted when it promoted that pin. The cases live on in `src/test/auditAccess.test.tsx`; the pointer was not moved with them.
opinion: Solid, and this is literally the codebase's own "client shows what the server refuses" principle, well tested and named by defect id.

title: Shift and break times: midnight, 24 hours and zero length

title: A product's colour can be set by the user

title: Reads page to exhaustion; no answer built on a short read

title: An operator's scope filters the roster only (D103, operators)

opinion: Correctly superseded by R-D109.

title: History keeps rendering a product it would no longer offer

title: A product colour is a palette token or one canonical hex

The client is lenient about what is typed (`#1BAF7A`, `1baf7a`, `#1ba`, padding) and strict about what it stores; a hex is a fill, never a text colour. One resolver, `src/lib/productColor.ts`, turns a stored colour into CSS.

title: The client's edit preview fails open; company-wide stays company-admin

title: Row controls carry accessible names unique to their row

title: Eligibility does not depend on what the caller may list

title: A row on a visible schedule stays readable (0026)

opinion: Correctly superseded by R-D109.

title: The board opens on the top of what you can see
claim: `visible_board_roots()` returns the nodes the caller can see whose parent they cannot — the real roots for a company or site admin, the department for a supervisor — never a node they could not SELECT. It runs as the caller and still scopes to one org for a session that bypasses RLS. Inactive tops are ordered last, not excluded.

title: The board header names the place; picker only with a choice
claim: The board reads "Board · <place> · <dates>"; a picker appears only when more than one root is offered. A remembered choice the server no longer offers is dropped, matching is exact (not ltree-prefix), and a person with no grant on any node sees a sentence about themselves rather than an error.

title: Split: the part record is company property, makers per plant

title: An assignment with no typed target shows what its cell's cycle time implies
source: the maintainer, 3 Sept (in session, "how much product can be made based on (how much time a person is assigned - breaks) / standard cycle time. This will become the default target for that assignment. This however can be overwritten by the already present mechanism") the maintainer, 3 Sept (in session, "when no cycle time are defined, the target for the assignment is null")
claim: An assignment carrying no explicit target_qty displays a DERIVED default: the minutes it covers, less the breaks of the shift pattern its cell resolves to, scaled by its efficiency, over the cell's seconds per unit. Whole units once one is achievable, one decimal below that — a 12 h cycle in an 8 h shift reads 0.7 rather than flooring to 0, because reporting nothing would read as impossible rather than as progress. NOTHING IS STORED: the value is recomputed on render, so a drag, a resize, a break edit or a re-pointed shift pattern is already right, and target_qty keeps its exact meaning as the human's override (R-031, R-313). No cycle time yields null, never zero, and the chip reads "target: NA" exactly as before.
